# criblio_guard_rule (Resource)

GuardRule Resource

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "criblio_guard_rule" "my_guard_rule" {
  context_keywords = [
    {
      keyword = "card"
      placement = "before"
    }
  ]
  description = "Sensitive data scanning (SDS) rule that detects credit card numbers in event data"
  group_id = "default"
  id = "credit-card-detection"
  regex = "/\\b(?:\\d[ -]*?){13,16}\\b/"
  rulesets = [
    "pci-compliance",
  ]
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tools/codegen -->
## Schema

### Required

- `group_id` (String) Worker group ID.
- `id` (String) Unique identifier for the SDS rule.
- `regex` (String) Regular expression pattern used to match sensitive data.
- `rulesets` (List of String) Rulesets that the rule belongs to.

### Optional

- `context_keywords` (Attributes List) Context keywords that help match sensitive data for this rule. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--context_keywords))
- `description` (String) Brief description of the SDS rule.
- `lib` (String) Name of the library that the rule belongs to.

<a id="nestedatt--context_keywords"></a>
### Nested Schema for `context_keywords`

Required:

- `keyword` (String) Keyword that provides additional context to help match sensitive data for the rule.

Optional:

- `placement` (String) Position of the keyword relative to the match: <code>before</code> or <code>after</code>.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, the [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) can be used with the `id` attribute, for example:

```terraform
import {
  to = criblio_guard_rule.my_criblio_guard_rule
  id = jsonencode({
    group_id = "default"
    id       = "employee_badge_id"
  })
}
```

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
terraform import criblio_guard_rule.my_criblio_guard_rule '{"group_id": "default", "id": "employee_badge_id"}'
```
